sections.heading: Follow one alarm from the sensor to the phone
sections.intro: Five steps, one manufacturer. Scroll to follow the signal, or select a step to see what happens and which DMP products do the work.

steps.label: Detect
steps.summary: Doors, windows, motion, smoke, glass and video.
steps.title: Detectors and cameras see the event
steps.body: Door and window contacts, motion and glassbreak detectors, smoke, heat and CO detectors and cameras all report to the panel, wired or over our 1100 Series wireless, which has been AES encrypted since 2019. AlarmVision analytics let cameras act like smart motion detectors.
receive: VUE Plus cameras and XV gateways

steps.label: Decide
steps.summary: XT, XTL and XR Series; XF6 for fire.
steps.title: The panel decides what the event means
steps.body: Cancel/Verify false alarm prevention has been a DMP feature since 2007. The XT75 runs intrusion, access control and AlarmVision together, and the XR550 supports 96 doors of access control.

steps.label: Report
steps.title: The signal goes out on more than one path
steps.body: We offer LTE, Wi-Fi and universal communicators, including the first alarm panel communicator for the AT&T FirstNet network (2020). The XR550 supports up to eight communication paths and moves to a backup path instantly. JamAlert detects cellular jamming, and VAULT encrypts the link to our cloud.

steps.label: Respond
steps.title: The monitoring center receives it
steps.body: At the central station a DMP receiver takes the signal. We introduced SCS-VR in 2009 as the first software-only central station receiver, and still offer SCS receivers and line cards.

steps.label: Control
steps.title: Owners and dealers stay in control
steps.body: Owners use Virtual Keypad on iOS, Android or the browser, and mobile wallet credentials such as Digital Key. Dealers program panels in bulk with Dealer Admin. Both cloud services are examined annually for SOC 2 Type II.

items: What is an access control system?
A system that decides who can open which door and when, and keeps a record. We make the controllers, readers, credentials and software for one.

Does access control work with the alarm?

Is there access control without a server?
The X1 Series is our stand-alone, cloud-based access control solution.

The 1164NS has the same functionality as the 1164 with synchronized sounders, minus the built-in sounder. It is meant for installations with existing sounder or notification devices.
What happens when one detector sounds?
It signals the panel to command all 1164s to sound. Any fire zone tripped on the panel also makes the sounders initiate.

sections.heading: Five answers dealers look up most: guides, glossary, codes and firmware
items: Where can I find installation, programming and user's guides?
In the documentation library, which also holds the General Troubleshooting Guide. Spec sheets, quick start guides, technical updates and more are there too.
How can I learn more about DMP and industry terminology?
DMP publishes a glossary of terms and definitions relevant to DMP and the security industry. Ask Technical Support at 888-436-7832 for the current link.
What is the code to get into Programming, Diagnostics and Keypad Options?

Programming: reset the panel by placing the reset jumper across the reset pins for two seconds, then removing it to one pin. At a keypad, press 6653 (PROG). XR Series panels need 6653 + CMD. If the keypad says ENTER CODE after you press PROG, enter the lockout code that the original installing company programmed. Diagnostics: reset the panel the same way, then at a keypad press 2313 (DIAG). XR Series panels need 2313 + CMD. The keypad screen displays DIAGNOSTICS. Keypad Options: on a 7800 Series keypad, scroll through the carousel menu and select Options, tap the wrench icon, press 3577 (INST) + CMD, then select KPD OPT to enter the keypad options menu.
What is the default user code?

Prior to 2020, the default user code for all panels was 99. As of 2020, the default user code is generated at DMP and printed on the box. Initializing user codes reverts the default code to 99. We strongly encourage every DMP dealer to change the user code once the installation is finished.
How do I update the firmware in my panel?

XTLplus/XTLtouch: update in Dealer Admin individually or with a Bulk Update over network or cell, or update directly with a 399 cable or 401 module. In Remote Link, set the Connection Type to Direct with a Baud Rate of 38400. XT30/XT50: update in Dealer Admin individually or with a Bulk Update over network or cell; the panel must be at Hardware Level M or higher to use Dealer Admin. You can also update directly with a 399 cable or 401 module, with Remote Link set to Direct at 38400. XT75: can only be updated in Dealer Admin, individually or with a Bulk Update. XR100/XR500: can be updated over network or serial. Serial connections can be made on the J22 header or the J21 DB9 connector with the J23 jumper set to R. XR350: serial connections can be made on the LX500 header. To enable the header, open the Diagnostics Menu by pressing 2313 (DIAG) + CMD, select PC Programmer and connect within 60 seconds. XR150/XR550: update in Dealer Admin individually or with a Bulk Update over network or cell. Serial connections can be made on the LX500 header, enabled the same way as on the XR350. XF6: can only be updated in Dealer Admin, individually or with a Bulk Update. iCom: update directly with a 399 cable or 401 module, with Remote Link set to Direct at 38400. CellCom/DualCom: update in Dealer Admin individually or with a Bulk Update over network or cell, or directly with a 399 cable or 401 module, with Remote Link set to Direct at 38400.

sections.heading: Programming doors, credentials and key fobs
items: How do I program the panel to disarm and gain access on a card swipe?

The 734 or module that controls the door must have the area the user wants to access and disarm programmed as the access area for the device in Device Setup. Users who swipe at the reader must also have a profile that can access and disarm that same area or areas.
Where do I program key fobs into the panel?

sections.heading: Reading the access denied messages
items: Why is the door not unlocking after presenting a credential to the reader?

These access denied messages appear in the panel event history. Invalid Code: the code read from the card does not match any user code in the panel. Invalid Time: access was attempted outside the schedule assigned to the user's profile. Invalid Area: the user attempted to access an area that is not defined in their profile. Invalid Level: door access is not enabled in the user's profile, or the system is in lockdown. Armed Area: the user attempted to access an armed area they do not have the authority to disarm. Inactive User: the user is marked as inactive in User Codes.

sections.heading: Codes, default users and who can change programming
items: What is the code to get into Programming, Diagnostics and Keypad Options?

Programming: reset the panel by placing the reset jumper across the reset pins for two seconds, then removing it to one pin. At a keypad, press 6653 (PROG). XR Series panels need 6653 + CMD. If the keypad says ENTER CODE after you press PROG, enter the lockout code that the original installing company programmed. Diagnostics: reset the panel the same way, then at a keypad press 2313 (DIAG). XR Series panels need 2313 + CMD. The keypad screen displays DIAGNOSTICS. Keypad Options: on a 7800 Series keypad, scroll through the carousel menu and select Options, tap the wrench icon, press 3577 (INST) + CMD, then select KPD OPT to enter the keypad options menu.
What is the default user code?

Prior to 2020, the default user code for all panels was 99. As of 2020, the default user code is generated at DMP and printed on the box. Initializing user codes reverts the default code to 99. We strongly encourage every DMP dealer to change the user code once the installation is finished.
What profile number is the default user code assigned to?

XR Series panels use profile numbers. The default user code is assigned to profile 99, the default master profile. XT Series and XTL Series panels use authority levels, and the default user code is assigned to the Master authority level.
Will DMP assist me with programming a panel?
DMP Technical Support is happy to answer your programming questions, but no DMP employee is permitted to change your programming.
Where do I find the panel firmware version?

The sticker on the panel shows the firmware it shipped with. For panels already installed, check XR Series panels under User Menu, System Status, and XT Series panels under Diagnostics, Panel Settings.

sections.heading: Firmware, Remote Link and communication paths
items: How do I update the firmware in my panel?

XTLplus/XTLtouch: update in Dealer Admin individually or with a Bulk Update over network or cell, or update directly with a 399 cable or 401 module. In Remote Link, set the Connection Type to Direct with a Baud Rate of 38400. XT30/XT50: update in Dealer Admin individually or with a Bulk Update over network or cell; the panel must be at Hardware Level M or higher to use Dealer Admin. You can also update directly with a 399 cable or 401 module, with Remote Link set to Direct at 38400. XT75: can only be updated in Dealer Admin, individually or with a Bulk Update. XR100/XR500: can be updated over network or serial. Serial connections can be made on the J22 header or the J21 DB9 connector with the J23 jumper set to R. XR350: serial connections can be made on the LX500 header. To enable the header, open the Diagnostics Menu by pressing 2313 (DIAG) + CMD, select PC Programmer and connect within 60 seconds. XR150/XR550: update in Dealer Admin individually or with a Bulk Update over network or cell. Serial connections can be made on the LX500 header, enabled the same way as on the XR350. XF6: can only be updated in Dealer Admin, individually or with a Bulk Update. iCom: update directly with a 399 cable or 401 module, with Remote Link set to Direct at 38400. CellCom/DualCom: update in Dealer Admin individually or with a Bulk Update over network or cell, or directly with a 399 cable or 401 module, with Remote Link set to Direct at 38400.
How do I connect to my panel with Remote Link?

XT30/50, XTL, XTLplus and XTLtouch: in Remote Link, set the Connection Type to Direct with a Baud Rate of 38400. These panels connect and program over network or cell, or by dialer on the XT30/50D, and a 399 cable or 401 module can update firmware directly. XR100/500: set the Connection Type to Direct with a Baud Rate of 9600. These panels connect over network, dialer, cell or serial. Serial connections must use the J22 header or the J21 DB9 connector with the J23 jumper set to R. XR150/350/550: set the Connection Type to Direct with a Baud Rate of 38400. These panels connect over network, dialer, cell or serial. Serial connections use the LX500 header with a 399 cable or 401 module; to enable the header, open diagnostics (2313 + CMD), select PC Programmer and connect within 60 seconds. CellCom/iCom/DualCom: set the Connection Type to Direct with a Baud Rate of 38400. These connect over cellular or network, and a 399 cable or 401 module can update firmware directly.
How do I program a Communication Path in my XR500 or XR150/350/550?

Program it in the Communication section of the panel programming menu. (1) Set the panel Account Number and press CMD until prompted to enter the Path Number. (2) Enter the Path Number and press CMD. (3) Use a top row select key or area to choose a Communication Type (None, DD for Digital Dialer, NET, CID for Contact ID, or press CMD to move on to CELL or WiFi). (4) Continue to configure the other settings for the path. (5) Enter the Phone Number (DD or CID) or IP Address (Net or Cell) of the Monitoring Center receiver. (6) Press CMD until STOP displays, then press a top row select key or area to save programming.
What firmware version do I need to install a cellular modem?
XT30/XT50 Control Panels: version 213 (4/12/22) and higher. XT75 Control Panels: all versions. XR150/550 Control Panels: version 213 (4/8/22) and higher. XF6 Series Fire Control Panels: all versions.
I am unable to connect to my system from Dealer Admin or Virtual Keypad. What should I check?
For systems connected over network, make sure the appropriate App Key is populated in Remote Options.

sections.heading: Wireless devices on the panel
items: What are the compatible wireless receivers for each DMP control panel?

Wireless Trouble means the panel and wireless receiver are not transmitting data back and forth. The on-board LEDs on the receiver verify power and communication (Power, RXD and TXD). On XR Series panels, the X-Bus Status option in the Diagnostics Menu (2313 + CMD) tests communication with the receiver. If a software version appears on the screen, the panel is communicating with the receiver. It is also possible that the tampers are not being depressed on the wireless receiver. The 1100X-W and 1100XH-W wireless receivers, which are compatible with any XR Series panel, have a case tamper and a wall tamper. Make sure both are depressed before you continue to troubleshoot. Note: Wireless Trouble does not show up for an issue with a wireless zone.
How many 1100R wireless repeaters do DMP panels support?
DMP panels support up to 8 repeaters.
Where do wireless zone numbers start on XR panels?
XR100/XR150: zones 500-599. XR500/XR550: zones 500-999. Note: watch for existing hardwired zones or hardwired outputs already programmed on the LX expansion bus.
Where do I program key fobs into the panel?
XT30/XT50: zone numbers 31-34 and 41-44. XTLplus/XTLTouch: zone numbers 51-54 and 61-64. XR100/XR500 and XR150/XR350/XR550: zone numbers 400-449.
Where do I install the wireless antenna on the XT50?

The XT50 wireless antenna terminal block is in the top right corner of the circuit board. The antenna installs through a small opening in the top of the enclosure and attaches to the panel at the right terminal. The left terminal is not used.
How do I clear a low battery message for wireless devices?
Replace the battery and perform a sensor reset by pressing Reset on a Touchscreen keypad or by pressing and holding the 2 key on a Thinline keypad.

sections.heading: Keypads, schedules, access and app connections
items: How do I address a keypad?

Thinline keypads: (1) Hold down the Back Arrow and CMD keys for two seconds. (2) At Set Brightness, enter 3577 + CMD. (3) Press the top row select key under KPD OPT to select Keypad Options. (4) Press any top row select key to clear the default keypad address, which is 01. (5) Enter the new keypad address and press CMD. (6) Program the keypad device number in Device Setup to match the new address. Touchscreen keypads: (1) Press Options in the carousel menu. (2) Press the Installer Options wrench icon. (3) Enter 3577 + CMD. (4) Press the top row select area under KPD OPT to select Keypad Options. (5) Press any top row select area to clear the default keypad address, which is 01. (6) Enter the new keypad address and press CMD. (7) Program the keypad device number in Device Setup to match the new address.
I want the panel to auto arm but not auto disarm. Do I need an opening time on the schedule?
Yes. You need an Open Time even if you are not automatically disarming. If you do not want the panel to disarm automatically, do not enable Auto Disarm.
How do I program the panel to disarm and gain access on a card swipe?

The 734 or module that controls the door must have the area the user wants to access and disarm programmed as the access area for the device in Device Setup. Users who swipe at the reader must also have a profile that can access and disarm that same area or areas.

Push notifications are enabled on the user's mobile device with the Virtual Keypad app. In Settings, the user chooses whether to receive push notifications for Alarms, Troubles and Arms/Disarms. Additional push notifications can be sent for Sensor Activity. That option only appears if it is enabled on the system in Dealer Admin, and users can receive sensor activity notifications from up to 50 different zones programmed into the panel. Push notifications follow the primary communication type set in Dealer Admin. If the system uses EasyConnect in Dealer Admin, the panel's main communication must be Network or WiFi and port 7001 TCP outbound must be open. If the system uses Cell in Dealer Admin, the panel's communication must be Cellular.
What do I need to program in my panel for EASYconnect App Connections?

Program the App Key in the Remote Options menu during panel programming. To find the App Key, each dealer can look at their Dealer Settings in Dealer Admin. EASYconnect connections are available on network XT Series panels with version 112 (10/5/2012), on XR150/550 panels and on XTLplus/XTLTouch panels. Port 4001 TCP must be open outbound. The App Key is not needed for cellular-only panels.

sections.heading: Address a keypad, update it, reach installer options.
sections.subhead: Firmware updates for the 5-Inch (7800/9800) and 7-Inch (8860) touchscreen keypads, keypad addressing and the installer code.

sections.heading: Updating keypad firmware
items: How do I update the firmware in my 5-Inch Graphic Touchscreen Keypad (7800/9800)?

Version 107 or later: (1) Download the firmware update from DMP's Product Software Downloads page. (2) Unzip the file onto a FAT32 formatted Micro-SD card. (3) Insert the card into the slot on the right of the keypad. (4) Power cycle the keypad or select Restart from the Keypad Options Menu. Version 106 or earlier: (1) Contact the Customer Repair Center. (2) Request an update to the latest firmware version. (3) Send the keypad in to DMP to be updated.
How do I update the firmware in my 7-Inch Touchscreen Keypad (8860)?

Update from Dealer Admin: (1) Make sure the keypad is connected to the Wi-Fi network. (2) Go to Dealer Admin. (3) Select the user and system. (4) Next to the keypad name, select Update. Update in Installer Options: (1) Make sure the keypad is connected to the Wi-Fi network. (2) Select Options from the carousel menu, then Installer Options. (3) Enter 3577 and press CMD. (4) Select Check for Updates and follow the on-screen prompts.

sections.heading: Addressing keypads and getting in
items: How do I address a keypad?

Thinline keypads: (1) Hold down the Back Arrow and CMD keys for two seconds. (2) At Set Brightness, enter 3577 + CMD. (3) Press the top row select key under KPD OPT to select Keypad Options. (4) Press any top row select key to clear the default keypad address, which is 01. (5) Enter the new keypad address and press CMD. (6) Program the keypad device number in Device Setup to match the new address. Touchscreen keypads: (1) Press Options in the carousel menu. (2) Press the Installer Options wrench icon. (3) Enter 3577 + CMD. (4) Press the top row select area under KPD OPT to select Keypad Options. (5) Press any top row select area to clear the default keypad address, which is 01. (6) Enter the new keypad address and press CMD. (7) Program the keypad device number in Device Setup to match the new address.
Why has the keypad stopped working after exiting Programming?

The most common cause is an address conflict with wireless zones that occupy the same address as the keypad. For example, the keypad is set at address 1 and wireless zones 11-14 were just added. Either change the keypad address or reprogram the zones at the next available address.
What is the code to get into Programming, Diagnostics and Keypad Options?

Programming: reset the panel by placing the reset jumper across the reset pins for two seconds, then removing it to one pin. At a keypad, press 6653 (PROG). XR Series panels need 6653 + CMD. If the keypad says ENTER CODE after you press PROG, enter the lockout code that the original installing company programmed. Diagnostics: reset the panel the same way, then at a keypad press 2313 (DIAG). XR Series panels need 2313 + CMD. The keypad screen displays DIAGNOSTICS. Keypad Options: on a 7800 Series keypad, scroll through the carousel menu and select Options, tap the wrench icon, press 3577 (INST) + CMD, then select KPD OPT to enter the keypad options menu.

sections.heading: Connecting the app and sending notifications
items: I am unable to connect to my system from Dealer Admin or Virtual Keypad. What should I check?
For systems connected over network, make sure the appropriate App Key is populated in Remote Options.

Push notifications are enabled on the user's mobile device with the Virtual Keypad app. In Settings, the user chooses whether to receive push notifications for Alarms, Troubles and Arms/Disarms. Additional push notifications can be sent for Sensor Activity. That option only appears if it is enabled on the system in Dealer Admin, and users can receive sensor activity notifications from up to 50 different zones programmed into the panel. Push notifications follow the primary communication type set in Dealer Admin. If the system uses EasyConnect in Dealer Admin, the panel's main communication must be Network or WiFi and port 7001 TCP outbound must be open. If the system uses Cell in Dealer Admin, the panel's communication must be Cellular.
What do I need to program in my panel for EASYconnect App Connections?

Program the App Key in the Remote Options menu during panel programming. To find the App Key, each dealer can look at their Dealer Settings in Dealer Admin. EASYconnect connections are available on network XT Series panels with version 112 (10/5/2012), on XR150/550 panels and on XTLplus/XTLTouch panels. Port 4001 TCP must be open outbound. The App Key is not needed for cellular-only panels.

sections.heading: Schedules, Remote Link and default codes
items: I want the panel to auto arm but not auto disarm. Do I need an opening time on the schedule?
Yes. You need an Open Time even if you are not automatically disarming. If you do not want the panel to disarm automatically, do not enable Auto Disarm.
Where do I download Remote Link software and updates?
Remote Link software is available for download in Dealer Admin under Resources, then Downloads.
What is the default user code?

Prior to 2020, the default user code for all panels was 99. As of 2020, the default user code is generated at DMP and printed on the box. Initializing user codes reverts the default code to 99. We strongly encourage every DMP dealer to change the user code once the installation is finished.

sections.heading: Digital Key privacy, firmware updates, SCS-1R and SCS-VR signals.
sections.subhead: What the Digital Key does and does not track, every panel firmware update path, Remote Link settings and the network traffic a receiver needs.

sections.heading: Digital Key privacy and revoking credentials
items: Will the DMP Digital Key track my personal data during the install or operations?

No. Adding and using the Digital Key in an Apple or Android Wallet requires a valid email address for wallet login validation and to email credential notifications. If credentials are distributed by SMS text, a mobile phone number is required.
Will the DMP Digital Key track my phone location?
No. DMP does not use or require location services to use the Digital Key.
Can the Digital Key be set up so that I do not have to unlock my phone?
Yes, by enabling the Mobile Wallet Express mode for the Digital Key credential.
How do I get the Digital Key back from a user that leaves the company?
Digital Keys are revoked and expired remotely in Virtual Keypad, without needing anything from the user.

sections.heading: Panel firmware and Remote Link
items: How do I update the firmware in my panel?

XTLplus/XTLtouch: update in Dealer Admin individually or with a Bulk Update over network or cell, or update directly with a 399 cable or 401 module. In Remote Link, set the Connection Type to Direct with a Baud Rate of 38400. XT30/XT50: update in Dealer Admin individually or with a Bulk Update over network or cell; the panel must be at Hardware Level M or higher to use Dealer Admin. You can also update directly with a 399 cable or 401 module, with Remote Link set to Direct at 38400. XT75: can only be updated in Dealer Admin, individually or with a Bulk Update. XR100/XR500: can be updated over network or serial. Serial connections can be made on the J22 header or the J21 DB9 connector with the J23 jumper set to R. XR350: serial connections can be made on the LX500 header. To enable the header, open the Diagnostics Menu by pressing 2313 (DIAG) + CMD, select PC Programmer and connect within 60 seconds. XR150/XR550: update in Dealer Admin individually or with a Bulk Update over network or cell. Serial connections can be made on the LX500 header, enabled the same way as on the XR350. XF6: can only be updated in Dealer Admin, individually or with a Bulk Update. iCom: update directly with a 399 cable or 401 module, with Remote Link set to Direct at 38400. CellCom/DualCom: update in Dealer Admin individually or with a Bulk Update over network or cell, or directly with a 399 cable or 401 module, with Remote Link set to Direct at 38400.
Where do I download Remote Link software and updates?
Remote Link software is available for download in Dealer Admin under Resources, then Downloads.
How do I connect to my panel with Remote Link?

XT30/50, XTL, XTLplus and XTLtouch: in Remote Link, set the Connection Type to Direct with a Baud Rate of 38400. These panels connect and program over network or cell, or by dialer on the XT30/50D, and a 399 cable or 401 module can update firmware directly. XR100/500: set the Connection Type to Direct with a Baud Rate of 9600. These panels connect over network, dialer, cell or serial. Serial connections must use the J22 header or the J21 DB9 connector with the J23 jumper set to R. XR150/350/550: set the Connection Type to Direct with a Baud Rate of 38400. These panels connect over network, dialer, cell or serial. Serial connections use the LX500 header with a 399 cable or 401 module; to enable the header, open diagnostics (2313 + CMD), select PC Programmer and connect within 60 seconds. CellCom/iCom/DualCom: set the Connection Type to Direct with a Baud Rate of 38400. These connect over cellular or network, and a 399 cable or 401 module can update firmware directly.

sections.heading: Receiving and acknowledging signals
items: What do I need to receive signals and acknowledge them with my SCS-1R or SCS-VR?

Your public IP address should receive signals on the port you choose in Communication programming, and those signals should route into your network to the correct SCS-1R Line Card or SCS-VR Group. The same ports should be open outbound for TCP so the receiver can respond to Network signals, and ALL UDP should be open outbound to acknowledge cellular signals, because of the way cellular communicates. Your SCS-1R or SCS-VR receiver also needs automation software so your Monitoring Center operator knows what signal came in, which system and who to contact. Direct automation questions to your automation company.

sections.heading: Wireless Trouble, zone numbers and 1100R repeaters, explained.
sections.subhead: What Wireless Trouble means, how to test every wireless zone, where zone numbers start on XR panels and which receiver goes with which panel.

sections.heading: Receivers, repeaters and zone numbers
items: What are the compatible wireless receivers for each DMP control panel?
How many 1100R wireless repeaters do DMP panels support?
DMP panels support up to 8 repeaters.
Do I program my wireless repeater as a device in Device Setup programming?

No. Repeaters are programmed as zones in the control panel. If several repeaters go on the same system, they must be programmed with sequential zone numbers. Program repeaters as Auxiliary Type zones, with the Disarmed Open and Disarmed Short messages set to Trouble and the Armed Open and Armed Short messages set to Alarm in Advanced Zone Programming.
Where do wireless zone numbers start on XR panels?
XR100/XR150: zones 500-599. XR500/XR550: zones 500-999. Note: watch for existing hardwired zones or hardwired outputs already programmed on the LX expansion bus.
Where do I install the wireless antenna on the XT50?

The XT50 wireless antenna terminal block is in the top right corner of the circuit board. The antenna installs through a small opening in the top of the enclosure and attaches to the panel at the right terminal. The left terminal is not used.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting and testing wireless
items: Wireless Trouble means the panel and wireless receiver are not transmitting data back and forth. The on-board LEDs on the receiver verify power and communication (Power, RXD and TXD). On XR Series panels, the X-Bus Status option in the Diagnostics Menu (2313 + CMD) tests communication with the receiver. If a software version appears on the screen, the panel is communicating with the receiver. It is also possible that the tampers are not being depressed on the wireless receiver. The 1100X-W and 1100XH-W wireless receivers, which are compatible with any XR Series panel, have a case tamper and a wall tamper. Make sure both are depressed before you continue to troubleshoot. Note: Wireless Trouble does not show up for an issue with a wireless zone.
How do I test my wireless zones?

There are two ways to test DMP wireless communication. Option 1, the wireless test: (1) Reset the control panel by shorting the RESET header or pressing the RESET button, depending on the panel. (2) At a keypad, press 8144 (WALK), then CMD on XR panels. (3) Press CMD until the WLS option displays and select it. This starts a wireless check-in test that runs for five minutes and checks the consistency of your signals. Zones that fail need to be relocated, or a repeater should be added. The panel shows how many transmitters are checking in, and when the test ends it shows which transmitters failed, if any. You can also run it in Dealer Admin under System Tests, Wireless Test. Option 2, the transmitter LED, built into all 1100 Series wireless products: with the cover removed, hold the transmitter in the desired location and press the tamper switch to send data to the panel. If communication is confirmed, the LED blinks immediately on and immediately off for each press or release of the tamper switch; repeat the test until you see five consecutive blinks. If communication is faulty, the LED stays on for about 8 seconds or flashes several times in quick succession. Relocate the transmitter or the wireless receiver until the LED confirms clear communication.
How do I clear a low battery message for wireless devices?
Replace the battery and perform a sensor reset by pressing Reset on a Touchscreen keypad or by pressing and holding the 2 key on a Thinline keypad.

sections.heading: Dealer Account and monthly Entré/SCS-VR support billing
items: How does monthly support billing work?

Effective August 1, 2022, all Entré and SCS-VR support is billed monthly. On the first day of each month, one invoice containing all active licenses is emailed to the dealer, the same way all other invoices are delivered. Each license has its own billing record on the invoice. Support is billed in advance, so August's invoice is for August support, and the monthly amount is the annual amount divided by twelve, rounded.

For new Entré or SCS-VR licenses, monthly support billing begins on the first day of the month after purchase. The first invoice contains a prorated amount from the purchase date to the end of that month, plus the current month. For example, for an Entré license bought July 20, no support is charged on the purchase invoice, and the August 1 invoice includes prorated support for July 21 to 31 plus the full month of August.
How is prepaid annual support shown?

Prepaid licenses show their billing details and support expiration date on each monthly invoice, with no monthly charge until support expires. In the month support expires, the amount billed is prorated from the expiration date to the end of the month.
Can dealers auto pay monthly invoices?

Yes. The email containing the monthly invoice has a link to sign up for and manage autopay by ACH or credit card, and it can be cancelled any time through the same link. Autopay applies only to software support invoices. Dealers on EFT terms should not use autopay for software support.
What are the payment terms, and who gets past due notices?

Payment terms for monthly support invoices are net 30. The only exception is EFT customers, whose terms are 15 days from the invoice date. All interested parties at the dealer receive past due notices, and dealer admin users or DMP accounts receivable can add interested parties under Users, then License Contacts, in Dealer Account.
How does a dealer cancel a software license?

Use the Software License Cancellation Acknowledgement form on the License tab in Dealer Account, or contact DMP accounts receivable at acctsrec@dmp.com. Once the form is signed, the license no longer receives support or software updates. A dealer who later needs support or updates must buy a new license.
Does free freight apply to my orders?

Enrolling in the Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) program makes all of your orders qualify for free freight. Orders larger than $1,500 qualify when the account is paid within 30 days, and column 4, 5 or 6 dealers qualify when the account is paid within 30 days. None of this applies to credit card terms.

sections.heading: Privacy Policy
sections.subhead: How we collect, use, disclose and protect Personal Information.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body:
Digital Monitoring Products (herein referred to as “Digital Monitoring Products”) appreciates that privacy is important to you and is committed to protecting the confidentiality of Personal Information and handling Personal Information with integrity and with an understanding of its sensitive nature. As such, Digital Monitoring Products has created this Privacy Policy (the “Privacy Policy” or the “Policy”), and all employees of Digital Monitoring Products are expected and required to abide by this Privacy Policy. This Privacy Policy applies solely to information collected by this website, except where stated otherwise.

For the purposes of this Policy, Personal Information is information that can be used to directly or indirectly to identify a living individual. Personal Information may include, but is not limited to, sensitive categories of information, herein referred to as Sensitive Personal Information, such as information that reveals racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, trade union membership, health, sexual or gender orientation.

This Policy is designed to protect Personal Information under applicable law as it exists. Digital Monitoring Products understands that laws and circumstances may change quicker than the Policy can be adjusted to fit and that this Privacy Policy cannot address every possible issue and circumstance. As such, this Privacy Policy is subject in all respects to local legal and regulatory requirements, as well as existing agreements, and Digital Monitoring Products confirms that the company will comply with any such requirements and existing agreements.

The Digital Monitoring Products web site at www.dmp.com (the “Site”) provides you with information about Digital Monitoring Products, its products and services, and in certain circumstances, allows you to purchase products or services or sign up to receive further information about Digital Monitoring Products. In order to provide you with access to this information about Digital Monitoring Products, and the ability to purchase products and services offered by or through the Site, certain Personal Information is collected from visitors to the Site. This Privacy Policy is designed to inform you about the types of information that are collected, as well as our use of such Personal Information, and sets forth the guidelines Digital Monitoring Products uses in protecting your privacy. This Privacy Policy applies to your use of the Site, any other Digital Monitoring Products site that is linked from www.dmp.com, as well as your use of Digital Monitoring Products’s social media web sites and pages, including without limitation, YouTube™, Facebook® , LinkedIn ® , Twitter® , Instagram® , and Google+™, which are all included in the definition of “Site”. This Privacy Policy shall also be deemed part of the Digital Monitoring Products Site Terms of Use.

This Privacy Policy describes the types of Personal Information that Digital Monitoring Products collects in connection with this Site. Digital Monitoring Products gathers Personal Information and will distribute this information only within Digital Monitoring Products in an effort to meet your needs and respond to your information requests.

We note that if you are a Digital Monitoring Products employee, contractor, supplier, customer or other partner, the use and protection of Personal Information may be subject to additional contractual obligations between us, including without limitation, additional Digital Monitoring Products policies.

sections.heading: Personal vs. Non-personal Information
sections.body:
Personal Information

Personal Information may be collected from you as you use the Site. Personal Information generally is information that personally identifies you in some way(s). Examples include your name, address, birth date, email address, phone number, other data collected when purchasing our products or services, education, employment, credit card, or other credit information. Additional examples include information submitted through our call centers, by joining a mailing list, by participating in social media events, contests or surveys, and signing up for email alerts or distributions. If during your visit to the this website you submit Personal Information to us, you are choosing to provide us with your Personal Information and you agree that it will be used to provide the information, products or services that you request (including information on additional products and or services which Digital Monitoring Products reasonably thinks may be of interest to you) and you consent to Digital Monitoring Products’s use of your personal information to improve or market Digital Monitoring Products’s products or services. Digital Monitoring Products does not knowingly request or collect Personal Information from any person under the age of 13 and we ask that any individual who is under the age of 13 to refrain from using our Site or submitting any Personal Information.

Non-Personal Information

Non-personal information includes general information about your visit to the Site that is not personal information or does not personally identify you. Digital Monitoring Products’s web server will recognize your domain name, which will be collected to monitor general use of the Site and for improvements to the Site, our products, and services. Similarly, cookies provide non-personal information which allows us to track the anonymous use of our Site, including use and traffic statistics each time you visit by placing small data files placed on your hard drive by the Site. Cookies also make the Site more convenient and easier to navigate for you, but they do not collect personal information. Cookies can be ‘session cookies’ (which are deleted when you close your browser) and/or ‘persistent cookies’ which remain on your computer for a longer period of time. Further detail on cookies is discussed below. You can disable or reject the use of cookies, by modifying the appropriate settings on your browser. Note that by doing so, however, you will likely not enjoy the full functionality of the Site.

sections.heading: Use, Disclosure and Protection of Personal Information
sections.body:
It is Digital Monitoring Products’s intention to obtain Personal Information only by fair and lawful means, and to use the Personal Information to service your needs and requests. Digital Monitoring Products will not process Personal Information in a manner incompatible with the purposes for which it was originally collected unless later authorized by the individual from whom the information was collection or unless allowed by law. We will not keep Personal Information longer than is necessary for the purposes for which it was originally gathered.

When do collect and process Personal Information about individuals, we will disclose certain information to those particular individuals on a reasonable and timely basis upon written request of the individuals from whom the Personal Information was collected. The disclosed information will include what Personal Information is being collected, who is collecting it, how and for what purposes it is being collected, how it is being us and to whom it is being disclosed. We will allow individuals reasonable access to their Personal Information to verify, correct or delete their data, where inaccurate.

We may also use Personal Information to process an order made through the Site, including shipping and returns of such order, and for organizing and submitting customer satisfaction reviews. We may also use such Personal Information to support marketing for our products and services and to enhance the content and use of our Site.

In order for Digital Monitoring Products to provide our products and services, we may need to share your Personal Information with other companies, agencies or contractors affiliated with Digital Monitoring Products. We will always seek to ensure that it is kept secure and only used in accordance with your instructions and agreed purpose.

Further, we may use and disclose Personal Information to the extent necessary to comply with laws, regulations, court orders, government agencies or investigations and similar legal instructions, to resolve disputes, and to protect Digital Monitoring Products rights and property.

Additionally, we may also contract with other third-parties to provide services, such as shipping, payment processing, contact verification, market research, and organization of promotions, or other subcontractors; however, we will provide these contractual parties only with the Personal Information necessary to perform the work for which they were contracted.

Digital Monitoring Products and its third-party providers may use cloud-based tools, and in such event, data might be processed in countries outside the United States. In such cases, Digital Monitoring Products and any such provider will agree to the necessary terms as required by law to protect Personal Information.

Digital Monitoring Products will process Personal Information only with consent and when such processing is permitted by applicable law. If Digital Monitoring Products needs to process Sensitive Personal Data, which is very rare, Digital Monitoring Products will obtain explicit consent for such processing, unless such processing is permitted by applicable law.

Digital Monitoring Products will not sell Personal Information to any third party and we will take commercially reasonable efforts to maintain the confidentiality of such information, in accordance with our contractual obligations as well as in compliance with those laws applicable in the states and countries in which we conduct business (and you should be aware that laws in all jurisdictions are not the same, and that some may have stricter requirements than others). Further, to protect your Personal Information from unauthorized access and use, Digital Monitoring Products maintains physical, electronic, and procedural safeguards, and requires those to whom we disclose Personal Information to do the same. We are committed to making sure that your Personal Information is accurate and up to date but it is your responsibility to let us know if your Personal Information is inaccurate or out of date and we can only make changes to your personal information if you notify us.

Digital Monitoring Products will retain your Personal Information only for so long as it is helpful to support the overall purpose for which we collected the information.

Digital Monitoring Products may use third party service providers, such as Google Analytics, to help analyze how users use the Site. By visiting this web site you are agreeing to our use of cookies for these purposes. For example, services like Google Analytics collect information anonymously and reports website trends without identifying individual visitors. Google Analytics collects only the IP address assigned to you on the date you visit the Site, rather than your name or other personally identifying information. Google Analytics uses cookies to collect information such as how often users visit the Site, what pages are visited, and what other sites are used prior to coming to the Site. Although Google Analytics plants a persistent cookie on your web browser to identify you as a unique user the next time you visit the Site, the cookie cannot be used by anyone but Google ® . Digital Monitoring Products does not combine the information collected through the use of Google Analytics with other personally identifiable information. Digital Monitoring Products uses the information we get from Google Analytics only to improve our Site and Services. Google’s ability to use and share information collected by Google Analytics about your visits to the Site is restricted by the Google Analytics Terms of Use, http://www.google.com/analytic... and the Google Privacy Policy, https://policies.google.com/privacy. If you are interested in learning about opting out of Google Analytics, visit: https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout.

pages.description: VAULT, Virtual Access Using Layered Tunneling, lets dealers and enterprises use Virtual Keypad and Dealer Admin without exposing systems to the public.
crumbs: DMP introduces VAULT: secure, encrypted connectivity for cloud-based security applications

sections.heading: VAULT: encrypted connectivity, no public internet exposure
sections.subhead: Secure access to cloud applications without exposing systems to the public internet.
sections.image_alt: The VAULT secure connectivity appliance graphic

sections.heading: A private, encrypted tunnel to SecureCom Wireless infrastructure
sections.body: Virtual Access Using Layered Tunneling (VAULT) is a secure communication platform that allows dealers and enterprise customers to use our cloud applications while keeping their security systems off the public internet. Organizations can use Virtual Keypad and Dealer Admin without exposing systems directly. VAULT creates a private, encrypted tunnel between a customer's corporate network and the SecureCom Wireless infrastructure, so systems reach our cloud services through a controlled and isolated connection.
bullets: Made for banks, financial institutions, government agencies and other organizations handling sensitive information
Keeps strict network boundaries in place

sections.heading: Six things VAULT does for an enterprise security network
items: Intrusion panels maintain encrypted communication with SecureCom servers.
Security systems remain isolated from the public internet.
Unlimited business panels managed through Dealer Admin.
Integrity checks and sequence numbering detect and block replay attacks or tampered packets in real time.
If a threat, breach or policy violation is detected, administrators can immediately terminate the VPN tunnel, isolating affected systems and preventing further access.

sections.heading: A point-to-point VPN built on AES, SHA and IKEv2
sections.body: VAULT operates as a point-to-point Virtual Private Network that secures IP communications using government-grade authentication and encryption. It supports established standards including the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) and Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA), while Internet Key Exchange (IKEv2) authenticates both endpoints and establishes the encrypted tunnel.
bullets: We provide a preconfigured VAULT appliance that streamlines deployment and integration
A VAULT spec sheet is available from DMP

sections.value: Our enterprise customers asked us for the highest grade of security for their businesses.

sections.heading: A global provider of software for security operations centers.
sections.body: SureView Systems is deployed across law enforcement, transportation, critical infrastructure and commercial organizations, and supports the largest integration library in the industry. It is built for organizations running their own security operations center, with a focus on financial services, critical infrastructure and technology companies. SureView is ISO 27001 certified. sections.heading: Two native components: alarm receipt and system sync.
sections.body: Alarms come from a DMP SCS-1R or SCS-VR receiver over a push-type connection on TCP port 9020 to a SureView Device Server or OpsLink Server. Zone, area, user and signal detail arrive attached, so a panic at a lobby door shows as that door, not a panel number. Areas, zones and devices configured in Entré populate SureView automatically, so nobody retypes a zone list into a second system. On arrival SureView Automate applies administrator rules to suppress predictable non-actionable alarms, escalate priority and route notifications. The event opens with its Action Plan, map position and nearby cameras streaming live and recorded video.

pages.description: The DMP 734A module and an Aperio AH30 Gen5 hub bring battery-powered Aperio locks into the familiar DMP control experience on XR150 and XR550 panels.

sections.heading: Up to 16 wireless locks on one hub.
sections.subhead: Our 734A Access Control Wireless Lock Integration Module and an Aperio AH30 Gen5 hub bring battery-powered Aperio locks into the familiar DMP control experience, managed from an XR150 or XR550 panel.
sections.image_alt: A hand holding a phone up to a door reader

sections.heading: A global leader in access solutions.
sections.body: ASSA ABLOY offers a broad portfolio of locking technologies for commercial facilities. Aperio wireless locking extends electronic access control to doors and other openings without wired connections at every lock. Through the DMP 734A module and the Aperio AH30 Gen5 RS-485 Communication Hub, compatible Aperio wireless locks work with XR150 and XR550 control panels while the customer keeps the DMP system and workflow they know.
bullets: Compatible Aperio wireless locks connect to XR150 and XR550 panels
Battery-powered locks simplify retrofits
Encrypted wireless communication between Aperio devices and the hub

sections.heading: Four links from credential to access decision.
sections.body: The XR150 or XR550 manages door access programming, users, credentials, permissions and schedules. The 734A connects the panel to the Aperio hub over a wired RS-485 link and passes access decisions between them. The AH30 Gen5 hub talks wirelessly to the locks. When a credential is presented, the lock sends it to the hub, the hub passes it to the panel through the 734A, and the panel checks it against its access programming before returning the decision. Lock setup, pairing and credential-reading settings are configured in the Aperio system, while door devices, users and permissions are programmed in DMP.
bullets: Each AH30 Gen5 hub supports up to 16 compatible wireless locks
The integration requires a compatible AH30 Gen5 hub
Aperio Privacy Mode and Escape and Return are not supported by the 734A integration
Real-time online communication, door status and audit activity, with remote lock and unlock response

Is the session a fixed script?

sections.heading: Four steps from the first call to a system you control
items: Tell us or a dealer what you need to protect: doors, alarm zones, cameras, fire. Our systems run intrusion, access control, fire and video.
We sell through authorized dealers and distributors. A dealer designs the system and installs it. Our Inside Sales team supports system design.
Dealers can lay out a system on a digital floor plan and produce a bill of materials, so you see what is going where.
Virtual Keypad runs on iOS and Android and in a browser. It arms and disarms the system and controls locks, lights and thermostats.

sections.heading: Six questions that separate a good proposal from a vague one
items: Which panel, and how many doors and zones does it support?
The XR550 supports 96 doors and 574 zones. The dealer should say which panel fits your building and why.
How does the system report an alarm?
Ask for the paths: network, cellular or both, and what happens when one fails.
Can my doors and my alarm be one system?
Intrusion and access control can share a panel, and one database manages credentials.
Can I use my phone as a key?
Digital Key puts a credential in a phone's mobile wallet, and it works even when the phone is out of power.
Who monitors it, and who do I call at night?
Ask who answers an alarm and who answers a service call, and at what hours.
What happens if I change dealers?
Ask who holds the programming and the customer account, and how it would be handed over.

pages.title: Which commercial intrusion panel fits which building | DMP
pages.description: How the XT50, XT75, XR150, XR550 and XR650 intrusion panels differ in zones, users, areas and doors, and which building each one fits.
crumbs: Which commercial intrusion panel fits which building

sections.heading: Which commercial intrusion panel fits which building?
sections.subhead: Five DMP panels, from the 58-zone XT50 to the XR650 with 300,000 user codes. Here is where each one belongs.

sections.heading: In brief
sections.body: Match the panel to the size and risk of the building. The XT50 and XT75 suit residential and small to medium business. The XR150 handles 142 inputs and 10,000 user codes. The XR550 reaches 574 zones and 96 doors, and the XR650, announced with availability to be confirmed, holds 300,000 user codes.

sections.heading: Which panel fits a small shop, office or home?
sections.body: The XT50 and XT75 are our hybrid panels for residential and small business. The XT50 supports 10 onboard zones plus 32 wired or 48 wireless, for up to 58 total zones, and it includes an onboard 1100D Series Wireless Receiver. It also carries one two-wire smoke detector zone and supports the Virtual Keypad app with daily opening and closing schedules. The XT75 does something different: it integrates intrusion, access control and AlarmVision on one network panel.
bullets: XT50: 99 user codes, six areas, eight doors of access, eight supervised keypads and a 200-event buffer
XT50: dialer or network communication now, with wireless or cellular (LTE) added later
XT75: three versions, the XT75, the XT75M in a medium enclosure and the XT75PCB, board only
XT75: listed for residential fire, residential burglary and commercial burglary

sections.heading: When does a building need an XR150?
sections.body: The XR150 is the step up when a commercial building outgrows a small-business panel. It has 142 inputs, including one built-in LX Bus with 100 zones, and eight keypads that give 32 zones. It supports 10,000 user codes with 99 profiles and up to eight doors of access. Relay outputs run from 2 to 106, and the panel includes a 50 VA transformer.
bullets: Eight areas and a 12,000 event buffer
Compatible with all 1100 Series Wireless and Keypads, including the 9800 Series
Supports the Virtual Keypad app
Dialer and network connectivity, with wireless or cellular added later

sections.heading: When does the XR550 earn its place?
sections.body: The XR550 is built for our most demanding commercial jobs and for large residential ones. It reaches 574 zones, 500 of them wireless, 32 areas and 16 supervised keypads. Doors of access start at 32 out of the box and reach 96. It also offers encrypted 10/100 network or Wi-Fi, LTE cellular or dialer communication, and relay outputs run from 2 to 506.
bullets: UL bank, safe and vault, Card Plus Pin and Dual Authority
Lockdown operation from a keypad or the app
99 assignable schedules for areas, doors and profiles
Remote flash update and programming
Adaptive Technology plus multi-lingual menus per user

sections.heading: What is the XR650 for, and can you order it yet?
sections.body: The XR650 is announced, and availability is to be confirmed. It is built for complex enterprise environments, with massive user capacity, advanced cybersecurity and IT-ready networking. It holds 300,000 user codes with 1,000 groups, up to 100 areas, 574 zones and 96 doors of access control. Bluetooth and mobile programming, a dual keypad bus and dual OSDP support make it easier to program.
bullets: XR-to-XR communication controls all XR panels from one keypad
Dual NIC keeps public network communication apart from a physically isolated network for video and access control devices
TLS 1.3, AES encryption and PKI with dual certificate trust domains
FIPS 140-3 is available with licenses

Dialer and network connectivity, with the option to add wireless or cellular later. Firmware version 263 added support for the 7883 Graphic Touchscreen Multi-Technology Keypad.
Encrypted 10/100 network or Wi-Fi, LTE cellular or dialer. The XR550 "E" versions use the encrypted network or Wi-Fi connection.
Dual NIC and dual-path IP plus Adaptive Technology. The communication path is always supervised, at minimal cellular cost.

pages.description: How an LTE alarm signal travels from the panel to the receiver, and how the 263LTE, 265LTE, CellCom and DualCom communicators differ.

sections.heading: How does cellular alarm communication work, and what are the options?
sections.subhead: An LTE communicator gives a panel a supervised path to the receiver. Which one you choose depends on the panel.

sections.heading: In brief
sections.body: A cellular communicator sends alarm messages from the panel over an AT&T or Verizon LTE network to a receiver. Choose the 263LTE for XT and XR panels, the 265LTE for XTL panels, and CellCom or DualCom to add a supervised path to other panels.

sections.heading: How does an alarm signal get from the panel to the receiver?
sections.intro: With our LTE communicators and SecureCom Wireless, the data goes straight to the DMP monitoring center receiver, with no network operations center in between.
nodes: An XT or XR Series panel, or another maker's panel with a universal communicator, raises the event.
The 263LTE on XT and XR panels, the 265LTE on XTL panels, or a universal CellCom or DualCom.
AT&T or Verizon carries the message. The 263LTE-FN is FirstNet Ready on AT&T.
Working with partner carriers, it sends the data directly to the DMP monitoring center receiver, without a network operations center.
A hardware or virtual receiver takes the alarm and supervision messages.

sections.heading: What does a dealer need to offer FirstNet Ready?
sections.body: The 263LTE-FN is approved for use on FirstNet, built with AT&T in a public-private partnership with the First Responder Network Authority. Alarm companies get Band 14, the nationwide spectrum the federal government set aside specifically for FirstNet. Dealers qualify in two steps, and the 263LTE-FN works only with XR Series panels.
bullets: First obtain a TMA Certificate of Verification
Then enter into a FirstNet Agreement with AT&T before offering FirstNet Ready panels with FirstNet service
With the XR150 or XR550 Series, a model 381 cable connects the cell module
It is made for DMP XR Series panels

sections.heading: How do you add cellular to someone else's panel?
sections.body: Use a universal communicator. CellCom provides a fully supervised alarm path over LTE, and with it almost every panel can use Virtual Keypad for arming, disarming and viewing up to six cameras. DualCom captures Contact ID messages from a panel's dialer output and sends them over a supervised path.
bullets: CellCom: program your own account number to work around locked panels
CellCom comes as the CELLCOM-2 and, for fire, the CELLCOMF-2, both DualSIM
DualCom puts primary network communication and LTE backup on one PCB
DualComNF is for fire, with primary network, secondary cellular and two sets of tip and ring terminals
DualComWZ is for residential, with primary Wi-Fi, secondary cellular and Z-Wave

sections.heading: What takes the signal at the other end?
items: Gives central stations computerized monitoring of DMP panels, with four digital dialer lines and one network line. It monitors dialer, LAN/WAN or internet accounts and shows a full English readout on every alarm message.

A UL Classified virtual receiver for network IP and cellular communications. Licensing runs from small organizations to those monitoring thousands of accounts, and one monthly invoice covers all active licenses.
The 263LTE and 265LTE are ready for activation with SecureCom Wireless, which also handles activation and billing for cellular service.
They follow the primary communication type set in Dealer Admin. If the system uses Cell, the panel's communication must be Cellular.

sections.heading: What is cloud-based access control, and what does a dealer need to know?
sections.subhead: The X1 is programmed in the cloud, Entré manages whole sites, and a phone can carry the credential.
sections.image_alt: The DMP X1 single-door access controller

sections.heading: In brief
sections.body: Cloud-based access control means doors are programmed and maintained through a hosted portal. Our X1 single-door controller is programmed in DMP's administrative portal and maintained in Virtual Keypad, with Digital Key and Mobile Bluetooth credentials for phones. Entré manages larger multi-site systems from a private network.

sections.heading: What makes the X1 cloud based?
sections.body: The X1 is a single-door access controller with an onboard network or Wi-Fi communicator. The X1 Series is fully programmed in DMP's administrative portal and maintained in Virtual Keypad. Its self-hosted EASYconnectAP Wi-Fi connection makes network and Wi-Fi settings easy to configure. Because it is a single-door controller, a site with several doors adds one controller per door.
bullets: Two reader inputs (in and out), a door position switch input, a request to exit input and a customizable input
Supports Wiegand and OSDP reader protocols
Optional LTE cellular module for primary or backup communications, and a module for PoE power
Wet or dry lock relay output option
Listed to UL Level I and Level IV

sections.heading: How does the X1 differ from Entré?
sections.intro: The X1 is cloud based. Entré runs across sites from a private network, with user management and report generation for XR Series panel users.
rows: DMP's administrative portal and Virtual Keypad
96, expandable to 400 doors and 500 panels with licenses

sections.heading: How do mobile credentials work?
sections.body: Phones can replace cards and fobs. A Digital Key credential sits in the mobile wallet of an NFC-enabled Android or iOS phone and works at the reader without the Virtual Keypad app, even when the phone has run out of power. A Mobile Bluetooth Credential loads on a Bluetooth Low Energy smartphone.
bullets: Both are nearly impossible to copy or clone
A lost credential is disabled immediately from Dealer Admin
Digital Key is managed in Virtual Keypad and Dealer Admin, and the Mobile Bluetooth Credential in Dealer Admin
The SR3 Bluetooth Reader reads Mobile Bluetooth Credentials and 125 kHz prox on one reader
The SR3 carries an IP67 rating and needs no special wiring

sections.heading: Which credential and reader does which job?
items: Android and iOS customers load a secure credential into the phone's mobile wallet. A smart watch with the credential in its mobile wallet gives a hands-free experience.

New users automatically get an email with instructions for adding Virtual Keypad and starting to use the credential. The expense and logistics of deploying traditional credentials are virtually eliminated.
One reader for phones and cards. It mounts on a wall or any suitable flat surface, indoors or out, and has a high degree of vandal resistance.
Four programmable zones and a 10 Amp Form C (SPDT) door strike relay, with a built-in piezo and a remote annunciation output.

sections.heading: What does a dealer need to know before specifying it?
sections.body: Check the readers first, then the communication path, then the software. The X1 supports Wiegand and OSDP reader protocols, and the 734N Network Access Control Module also takes Wiegand or OSDP readers over pre-wired network cabling. The 734 series supports OSDP and comes as the 734, the 734B BIN code, the 734N and the 734N-POE.
bullets: Entré Version 9.8.9 goes to dealers who bought an Entré license, are current on their support agreement and have an Entré Certified Technician
Entré works with XR Series control panels, and comes in Lite, Business and Enterprise editions
Add an LTE module to an X1 when cellular should be primary or backup communication
Entré add-ons come as 10 or 100 panel licenses and 4, 16, 32, 64 or 128 door licenses

sections.heading: How does a dealer run it day to day?
sections.body: Dealer Admin is our cloud-based portal for managing a dealer's business and customers' DMP panels. Virtual Keypad handles the user side. The customer dashboard shows each user's location, system type, version and connection method, and Dealer Admin also offers a custom referral program. When you add a user and assign a Digital Key credential in Virtual Keypad, the new user gets instructions by text or email for adding it to their mobile wallet.
bullets: Custom Roles give staff only the authority they need
Single Sign-On is an option
Reports, analytics and dashboards help you spot trends
Bulk remote updates and mass programming changes, with system health on one dashboard
Dealer Admin and Virtual Keypad are examined every year for SOC 2 Type II

sections.heading: How do you add video verification to an alarm system?
sections.subhead: Cameras, an AlarmVision gateway and a panel turn a motion alarm into something a person can see and confirm.

sections.heading: In brief
sections.body: Add cameras that work with the alarm, then let a person confirm what they see. An XV Gateway with AlarmVision joins cameras, analytics and an XT75 or XR Series panel. Virtual Keypad lets users view live footage and confirm Real Alarm or False Alarm. Evolon adds live operators.

sections.heading: What does video verification mean on an alarm system?
sections.body: It means someone can see what set off the alarm before deciding what to do. In Virtual Keypad, a user who gets an alarm notification can tap it, view live camera footage and confirm with Real Alarm or False Alarm. The VUE Video Doorbell works directly with monitoring station software, so operators can view video footage during an alarm. The doorbell gives a vertical view of visitors and packages, at 5MP / 3K resolution and a 9:16 aspect ratio.
bullets: Virtual Keypad asks "Is This A False Alarm?" when a system is in alarm
Operators get faster, more informed responses when video is part of the alarm
Live video, cloud clips and push notifications arrive once a VUE Plus camera is added in Dealer Admin
Actions can record clips on events such as Armed, Disarmed, Access Granted or Access Denied

sections.heading: What does AlarmVision add to a panel?
sections.body: AlarmVision integrates cameras, analytics and XT75 or XR Series control panels in one platform. It creates smart motion detectors that trigger panel responses and alarms in real time, with loitering, person, vehicle and animal analysis and detection. The gateways turn your customers' cameras into a crime deterrent tool, so they know their property is actively monitored.
bullets: Supports ONVIF and RTSP cameras, and is NDAA compliant
Up to four detection regions per camera
Two-way audio with ONVIF-compliant IP speakers
1 TB to 4 TB of internal storage, with a timeline to view bookmarked recordings

sections.heading: Which of our cameras can a dealer pair with it?
sections.intro: The gateways come as the XV-24 (24MP, single NIC), the XV-60 (60MP, dual NIC) and the XV-96 (96MP, dual NIC). Our cameras are below.
rows: Indoor and outdoor, including open floor retail and industrial

sections.heading: Can you verify with cameras the customer already owns?

Evolon, one of our six technology partners, offers its Proactive Video Monitoring Service, which works with DMP intrusion panels and AlarmVision and activates the camera infrastructure a site already has, so no new hardware is needed.
bullets: Evolon provides 24/7 live response from a U.S.-based Security Operations Center
No special licensing or dealer certification is required to offer the integration
Evolon services are sold as monthly or annual subscriptions
A dedicated Evolon partner portal holds installation guides, configuration documentation and support resources

crumbs: What SOC 2 Type II means for a security platform

sections.heading: What does SOC 2 Type II mean for a security platform?
sections.subhead: We share what our own examination covers: Dealer Admin and Virtual Keypad, examined every year.
sections.image_alt: A glowing shield with a padlock

sections.heading: In brief
sections.body: A SOC 2 Type II examination is an independent look at a company's controls. We complete one every year, conducted by a licensed CPA firm to AICPA standards, for Dealer Admin and Virtual Keypad. The SOC 3 report is intended for public distribution, and SOC 2 reports go to customers and partners under confidentiality.

sections.heading: What does our SOC 2 Type II examination cover?
sections.body: It covers Dealer Admin and Virtual Keypad, our SaaS applications, which are hosted within a Tier 4 data center. Tier 4 is designed to host mission-critical servers with fully redundant subsystems and compartmentalized security zones. Dealer Admin is a cloud-based portal for managing a dealer's business and customers' DMP panels. Virtual Keypad lets customers manage their systems from a computer, tablet or smartphone. For the formal definition of the criteria, the AICPA is the authority, so this article speaks only to what we have stated about our own examinations.
bullets: Tier 4 means fully redundant cooling, power, network links and storage
Both are examined independently each year
Compartmentalized security zones are part of the Tier 4 design
Dealer Admin has a Single Sign-On option and Custom Roles for staff
This article makes no claim about other products

sections.heading: Who examines it, and how often?
sections.body: A licensed CPA firm conducts the examination, in accordance with standards established by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA). We complete it annually, so a dealer or building owner is not relying on a single result from the past.
bullets: Independent: a licensed CPA firm conducts it
Annual: we complete an examination every year
Reports: a public SOC 3 report and confidential SOC 2 reports
Standards: those established by the AICPA

sections.heading: What is covered, at a glance?
sections.intro: These are the facts we state about our examination.
rows: The SOC 3 report is intended for public distribution
SOC 2 reports go to customers and partners under confidentiality
Dealer Admin manages a dealer's business and customers' DMP panels. Virtual Keypad lets customers manage their systems from a computer, tablet or smartphone.

sections.heading: Who can see the reports?
sections.body: There are two. The SOC 3 report is intended for public distribution. SOC 2 reports are available to customers and partners under appropriate confidentiality arrangements. That gives a specifier a public document to start with and a confidential one to request. Ask early if a project needs the SOC 2 report, because it is shared under confidentiality arrangements rather than published.
bullets: SOC 3: intended for public distribution
SOC 2: customers and partners, under confidentiality
Inside Sales, 877-757-4367, can route the question

sections.heading: What do Dealer Admin and Virtual Keypad actually do?
items: Dealer Admin performs bulk remote updates and mass programming changes, with system health status on a single dashboard.
Custom Roles grant staff only the authority they need to serve customers, but nothing more.
It enhances security and reduces time spent managing passwords and usernames.
When a system is in alarm, Virtual Keypad users tap the notification, view live camera footage and confirm Real Alarm or False Alarm.
On XR Series, the system manager can create up to 99 profiles and assign each user to up to four of them.
Temporary XT and XTL users are deleted automatically after seven days.

sections.heading: What should a specifier ask for?
sections.body: A short list turns the examination into something a project can use. Ask which applications the project depends on, then ask for the reports that fit.
bullets: Ask which of our applications the project will use: Dealer Admin, Virtual Keypad or both
Ask for the SOC 3 report, which is intended for public distribution
Ask for the SOC 2 report under confidentiality when the project needs more detail
Ask where the software is hosted: within a Tier 4 data center
Ask about the equipment separately, because product pages carry their own listings and certifications
Ask whether the project will carry phone credentials, which are managed in Dealer Admin and Virtual Keypad

sections.heading: What else does a security platform need around it?
sections.body: A SOC 2 examination speaks to hosted software. Building security also depends on the equipment on the wall. Where our product pages state them, these are the protections around the platform. Each is stated on its own product page.
bullets: 263LTE communicators carry NIST AES certification, #2350 128-bit and #2595 256-bit
The XR550 offers encrypted 10/100 network or Wi-Fi communication options
The SCS-1R and SCS-VR receivers carry NIST AES certification
JamAlert is UL 2610 certified

The XR650, announced with availability to be confirmed, lists TLS 1.3, AES encryption and PKI with dual certificate trust domains, with FIPS 140-3, 802.1x network authentication and Active Directory client integration available with licenses

pages.title: What to know before a wireless security retrofit | DMP
pages.description: Which 1100 Series receiver fits which panel, how the 1100T translator keeps other makers' devices, and how to test wireless signals before you drill.
crumbs: What to know before a wireless security retrofit

sections.heading: What should you know before a wireless security retrofit?
sections.subhead: Two-way, supervised 900 MHz devices add zones without new wire. Test the signal before the first screw.

sections.heading: In brief
sections.body: Pair the right receiver with the panel, keep working devices where you can, and test every location. Our 1100 Series is two-way and supervised on 900 MHz. The 1100T translator learns up to 128 zones from other makers' transmitters, and the panel's wireless test checks signals before you commit.

sections.heading: Which wireless receiver goes with which panel?
sections.body: The 1100 Series uses two-way, supervised 900 MHz frequency-hopping spread-spectrum technology. The receiver follows the panel: XT30 and XT50 panels use the 1100DH, and XT75, XR150 and XR550 panels use the 1100XH. The XT50 also includes an onboard 1100D Series Wireless Receiver.
bullets: The 1100XH supports up to 500 wireless transmitters
It adds transmit and receive amplification for greater distance or harsh building environments, and mounts near the panel enclosure or in a remote location
With version 210/310 firmware, up to 16 repeaters connect to an XR Series panel, up from eight, and transmitters connect to a nearby receiver or repeater more quickly
Watch for hardwired zones or outputs already programmed on the LX expansion bus

sections.heading: Can you keep the wireless devices already on the wall?
sections.body: Yes, for the makers it supports. The 1100T Wireless Translator upgrades non-DMP systems with one-way, low-frequency wireless transmitters, including Interlogix, Honeywell 5800, 2GIG and DSC. It talks to a DMP panel through an 1100 Series receiver's wireless connection, so there is no new wiring.
bullets: One 1100T can learn in up to 128 zones
Existing transmitters keep sending supervision and low battery messages to the panel
The 1100TF adds 24-hour standby battery backup
Certified for commercial and residential smoke detection

sections.heading: How do receivers, key fobs and zone numbers line up by panel?
sections.intro: Wireless zone numbers and key fob zones differ by panel, so check them before you program.

sections.heading: Which devices cover the usual retrofit jobs?
items: Two internal magnetic reed switches and an onboard terminal block give two independent zones from one transmitter. It includes a 3V lithium battery (CR123).
Fully supervised, low-current shock and glassbreak sensing, up to 20 feet from framed glass mounted in an outside wall.
Made for installation under the counter, with programmable LED feedback when a panic alarm is sent. The 1142BC version has a belt clip.
A battery-powered photoelectric detector with a synchronized sounder. When one sounds, the panel commands all 1164s to sound. Up to 572 units on one system.

sections.heading: How does a retrofit handle wireless smoke detection?
sections.body: The 1164 is a battery-powered wireless photoelectric smoke detector with an integrated synchronized sounder. It uses our 900 MHz two-way wireless technology, which has been approved for commercial fire applications since 2009. Any fire zone tripped on the panel makes the sounders sound, and the panel can trigger wired strobes and strobe horns.
bullets: Up to 572 units on one system
Listed to ANSI/UL 268, 7th Edition, with CSFM and FDNY listings
The 1164NS has the same functionality without the built-in sounder, for sites with existing sounders or notification devices
Models are the 1164-W wireless smoke detector and the 1164NS-W with no sounder

sections.heading: How do you test the signal before you drill?
sections.body: Run the panel's wireless test, from a keypad or in Dealer Admin under System Tests, Wireless Test. It starts a five-minute check-in test that checks the consistency of your signals, and at the end it shows which transmitters failed.
bullets: Zones that fail need to be relocated, or a repeater should be added
The other way is the LED built into every 1100 Series transmitter: with the cover removed, press the tamper switch and look for five consecutive blinks
If the LED stays on for about eight seconds or flashes several times in quick succession, relocate the transmitter or the receiver

sections.heading: What causes the usual surprises after install?
sections.body: Four things are worth planning for.
bullets: Wireless Trouble means the panel and receiver are not transmitting data back and forth; check that the case tamper and wall tamper on the receiver are depressed
A keypad that stops working after programming may share an address with wireless zones added at the same address
Repeaters are programmed as zones, with sequential zone numbers when there are several
A low battery message clears after you replace the battery and perform a sensor reset
On the XT50, the wireless antenna terminal block is in the top right corner of the circuit board, and the left terminal is not used
